meta.title: Documented indoor respiratory outbreaks for validating the lattice random-walk SIR model
meta.conventions: n_exposed/n_infected exclude the index case unless includes_index is true; None = not reported in the sources accessed; fields listed in `derived` are computed here, everything else is transcribed.

records.setting: Call centre, 11th floor of a 19-storey mixed-use building (open-plan desks)

sources.access: full text (Europe PMC OA XML) + Fig. 1/2 images (EID)
sources.citation: Park SY, Kim YM, Yi S, Lee S, Na BJ, Kim CB, et al. Coronavirus Disease Outbreak in Call Center, South Korea. Emerging Infectious Diseases. 2020;26(8):1666-1670. doi:10.3201/eid2608.201274

records.exposure_type: repeated daily co-working, multi-generation (onsets 25 Feb - 20 Mar on 11th floor)
records.exposure_duration_note: working days over ~2 weeks; hours per day not reported
records.geometry_note: Scaled floor plan published (Fig. 2) but no scale bar or area; 199 workstation desks digitized in two wings (137 north, 62 south) plus un-digitized east offices
records.ventilation: not reported (an 'evaluation of ventilation system' is marked on the epidemic curve but no results are given)
records.index_case: unknown; first 11th-floor onset 25 Feb 2020; an earlier 10th-floor case had onset 22 Feb
records.spatial_pattern: 'Most of the case-patients on the 11th floor were on the same side of the building'. Digitized Fig. 2: 79/137 desks marked as case seats in north wing vs 4/62 in south wing, 1 in east offices (84 marked seats vs 94 reported cases).
records.other_groups: Other floors: 7th 0/182, 8th 0/207, 9th 1/206, 10th 2/27, floors 1-6 0/84, residents 0/201. Household SAR 34/225 (15.1%); 34/210 (16.2%) for symptomatic index.
records.quality_notes: Attack rate denominators complete (99.8% tested). No room size, no ventilation, no hours. Seat map shows only 84 of 94 case seats; desk occupancy assumed 1 per desk. Multi-generation: not a single-source event.

model_mapping.lattice: 28 x 28 desk-pitch units (floor plan 900 x 897 px, desk pitch 32.5 px); physical pitch not reported (plausibly 1.0-1.6 m), central service core = obstacle block
model_mapping.T_days: 11-12 working days x ~8 h (21 Feb - 8 Mar 2020); multi-generation
model_mapping.index_position: unknown (seed anywhere in north wing; marginalise)
model_mapping.mobility: seated at desk (W zone), corridors, shared lobby/elevators
observables: other floors as negative control (1/595 on floors 7-9)
model_mapping.role: held-out multi-generation test (day-scale SIR is appropriate here)
model_mapping.obstacles: no room scale, no ventilation, no hours; SIR lacks a latent period although onsets are delayed ~5 d; 10 of 94 cases have no seat

records.setting: 13-person team in a 700 m2 open-plan office (team occupies about one quarter) + 30 m2 conference room

sources.citation: Weissberg D, Böni J, Rampini SK, Kufner V, Zaheri M, Schreiber PW, et al. Does respiratory co-infection facilitate dispersal of SARS-CoV-2? investigation of a super-spreading event in an open-space office. Antimicrobial Resistance & Infection Control. 2020;9(1):191. doi:10.1186/s13756-020-00861-z

records.exposure_type: single index, ~1.5 working days incl. a 1-h team meeting with singing
records.exposure_duration_note: index spent ~8 h presymptomatic + ~3 h oligosymptomatic with the team
records.room_dimensions: open-plan office 700 m2 (team area ~1/4); conference room 30 m2
records.geometry_note: workstations a minimum of 0.8 m apart; seating plan in Fig. 1 of source
records.ventilation: mechanical; 'air renewal within 1 hour' in open office (~1 ACH), within 15 min in conference room (~4 ACH); no recirculation
records.attack_rate_reported: index 'directly infected 67 to 83% of teammates' (8 or potentially 10 of 12); 11 of 13 team members ill overall
records.spatial_pattern: whole team affected; no gradient analysable (n=12, frequent shared-desk work, 5-min daily huddle)
records.quality_notes: Small n. Close-contact behaviour (shared keyboards, huddles, singing) confounds distance. 8 vs 10 secondary cases depends on generation assignment.

model_mapping.lattice: 9 x 9 (175 m2 team area ~ 13.2 m square) + conference room 4 x 4 (30 m2)
model_mapping.T_days: 11 h = 0.46 d (single index, first generation only)
model_mapping.role: held-out level test (overall attack rate)

records.setting: Public-facing public-sector office: three large open-plan offices over three storeys

sources.citation: Nicholls G, Atkinson B, van Veldhoven K, Nicholls I, Coldwell M, Clarke A, et al. An outbreak of SARS-CoV-2 in a public-facing office in England. Occupational Medicine. 2024;74(7):475-485. doi:10.1093/occmed/kqad100

records.exposure_type: multi-week workplace outbreak, multi-generation
records.ventilation: 'deemed adequate using carbon dioxide monitoring (typically <=1000 ppm)'
records.attack_rate_reported: 55% (22/40 workers)
records.spatial_pattern: surface contamination concentrated in a small shared security office (6/9 samples positive)
records.quality_notes: Abstract only; denominators include index; no geometry. Useful as a contrast: adequate ventilation + vaccination and still 55%.

model_mapping.role: qualitative only

records.setting: Beef-processing line, fixed work stations on a conveyor line (indoor workplace analogue with seat-like fixed positions)

sources.access: full text (Europe PMC OA XML); Appendix tables not retrieved
sources.citation: Günther T, Czech‐Sioli M, Indenbirken D, Robitaille A, Tenhaken P, Exner M, et al. SARS‐CoV‐2 outbreak investigation in a German meat processing plant. EMBO Molecular Medicine. 2020;12(12):e13296. doi:10.15252/emmm.202013296

records.exposure_type: single index, 3 consecutive shifts
records.exposure_duration_note: 3 shifts (shift length not stated; breaks 2x30 min + 1 h)
records.room_dimensions: processing line ~32 m x 8.5 m inside a 2,800 m2, 6.1 m high hall
records.geometry_note: distance of every fixed-position worker from the index plotted in source Fig. 3A (not digitized)
records.ventilation: air exchange rate < 1 per h for the hall; unfiltered recirculating cooling fans, ~10 C
records.masks: not stated as worn at the line in the text accessed
records.attack_rate_reported: 20/78 = 25.6% among workers with fixed stations around the index; '>60% of co-workers within a distance of 8 m' (counts in Appendix Table S2)
records.spatial_pattern: Spatial over-representation of cases maximal within an 8 m radius of the index (P = 2.3e-5); infection rates highest closest to the index.
records.other_groups: whole early shift: 18 positive of 140 tested on 25 May + 11 more in follow-up among 147 workers
records.quality_notes: Counts within 8 m not transcribed (appendix). Cold, recirculated air and heavy physical work: extrapolation to offices is qualitative only.

model_mapping.lattice: 21 x 6 (32 m x 8.5 m line area)
model_mapping.T_days: 3 shifts (~8 h each) = ~1 d of contact; first generation
model_mapping.index_position: known to authors (proximal half), not public
observables: radial profile of cumulative attack rate vs distance (source Fig. 3B, to be digitized)
model_mapping.role: held-out shape test (distance kernel) once Appendix Table S2 is transcribed
model_mapping.obstacles: index position withheld; cold recirculated air unlike an office

records.setting: Office building, co-workers of a cavitary tuberculosis case (classic Wells-Riley calibration)

sources.citation: Nardell EA, Keegan J, Cheney SA, Etkind SC. Airborne Infection: Theoretical Limits of Protection Achievable by Building Ventilation. American Review of Respiratory Disease. 1991;144(2):302-306. doi:10.1164/ajrccm/144.2.302

records.exposure_type: single index, ~4 weeks of co-working
records.ventilation: ~15 cfm (7 L/s) outdoor air per occupant; CO2 ~1000 ppm
records.attack_rate_reported: 27/67 (40%) tuberculin conversions
records.spatial_pattern: not reported in abstract
records.quality_notes: Different pathogen (obligate airborne). Abstract only. Included because it is the canonical office-scale calibration of the Wells-Riley equation that defines the quantum.

model_mapping.role: qualitative only (different pathogen)

records.setting: Supermarket (employees vs customers)

sources.citation: Tian S, Wu M, Chang Z, Wang Y, Zhou G, Zhang W, et al. Epidemiological investigation and intergenerational clinical characteristics of 24 coronavirus disease patients associated with a supermarket cluster: a retrospective study. BMC Public Health. 2021;21(1):647. doi:10.1186/s12889-021-10713-z

records.exposure_type: employees: repeated daily shifts (multi-day); customers: single short visits
records.exposure_duration_note: not reported (customer dwell time not measured)
records.ventilation: not reported
records.index_case: not identified with certainty; first-generation cases were employees
records.attack_rate_reported: employees 9.2% (11/120); customers 0/8224 screened; total screened 8437
records.spatial_pattern: none reported
records.quality_notes: Best available supermarket record: both employee and customer denominators. No geometry, no dwell times; the 11 employee cases include the unidentified primary case(s). Customer screening completeness not stated.

model_mapping.lattice: scene default 25 x 15 (store size not reported)
model_mapping.T_days: customers: one visit (scene dwell 27 min = 0.019 d); staff: daily shifts over >= 1 week
model_mapping.mobility: customers walking (Robin in/out boundary); staff semi-fixed
model_mapping.role: negative control for short-dwell risk + level test for staff
model_mapping.obstacles: no geometry, no dwell times, primary case unidentified

records.setting: Department store (retail floor, sales staff vs customers)

sources.citation: Chen T, Guo S, Zhong P. Epidemic characteristics of the COVID-19 outbreak in Tianjin, a well-developed city in China. American Journal of Infection Control. 2020;48(9):1068-1073. doi:10.1016/j.ajic.2020.06.006

Li W, Gong J, Zhou J, Fan H, Qin C, Gong Y, et al. The Analysis of Patterns of Two COVID-19 Outbreak Clusters in China. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. 2022;19(8):4876. doi:10.3390/ijerph19084876

Jiang G, Wang C, Song L, Wang X, Zhou Y, Fei C, et al. Aerosol transmission, an indispensable route of COVID-19 spread: case study of a department-store cluster. Frontiers of Environmental Science & Engineering. 2021;15(3):46. doi:10.1007/s11783-021-1386-6

records.exposure_type: staff: daily shifts over ~1 week; customers: single visits during Spring Festival shopping
records.ventilation: described as 'a poorly ventilated public place' (no measurement)
records.attack_rate_reported: no attack rate printed; staff cases 6 (Li 2022) or 7 (Chen 2020); 'approximately 200 employees', 194 employees isolated
records.spatial_pattern: none reported
records.other_groups: customer cases 23 (Li 2022) or 21 (Chen 2020), customer denominator unknown; 43-60 cases linked in total depending on cut-off date
records.quality_notes: Sources disagree on counts (6 vs 7 staff; 21 vs 23 customers; 43 vs 60 linked cases). Customer denominator absent, so no customer attack rate can be formed. Staff attack rate is DERIVED here.

model_mapping.lattice: 29 x 29 if the 3,400 m2 floor is taken as square (shape not reported)
observables: ratio of customer to staff cases 21-23 : 6-7 (no customer denominator)
model_mapping.role: qualitative / order-of-magnitude level check
model_mapping.obstacles: inconsistent counts across sources; no customer denominator

records.setting: Shopping mall, 8 floors; office on floor 7 plus retail floors B1-6

sources.citation: Cai J, Sun W, Huang J, Gamber M, Wu J, He G. Indirect Virus Transmission in Cluster of COVID-19 Cases, Wenzhou, China, 2020. Emerging Infectious Diseases. 2020;26(6):1343-1345. doi:10.3201/eid2606.200412

records.exposure_type: multi-day, mixed staff/customers, indirect contact
records.ventilation: not reported
records.index_case: uncertain (patient A, returned from Wuhan 18 Dec 2019)
records.attack_rate_reported: no denominators: 7 cases in one floor-7 office, 7 mall staff (floors B1-3), 10 customers, 11 close contacts
records.spatial_pattern: cases on several floors without direct contact; shared restrooms/elevators
records.quality_notes: Case series without denominators: cannot be used for attack rates; documents that retail transmission to customers occurs.

observables: existence of customer infections without direct contact
model_mapping.role: qualitative only

records.setting: Single grocery retail store, employees (cross-sectional PCR screen)

sources.citation: Lan FY, Suharlim C, Kales SN, Yang J. Association between SARS-CoV-2 infection, exposure risk and mental health among a cohort of essential retail workers in the USA. Occupational and Environmental Medicine. 2021;78(4):237-243. doi:10.1136/oemed-2020-106774

records.exposure_type: occupational, cumulative; point prevalence not an attack rate
records.ventilation: not reported
records.attack_rate_reported: 21/104 (20%) PCR-positive; customer-facing roles OR 5.1 (95% CI 1.1-24.8)
records.spatial_pattern: risk gradient by role (customer-facing vs not), not by position
records.quality_notes: Point prevalence in a high-incidence community; not attributable to in-store transmission. Use only as an upper bound on staff infection.

model_mapping.role: qualitative only

records.setting: Elementary-school classroom, 24 students in 5 rows, teacher reading aloud unmasked

sources.citation: Lam-Hine T, McCurdy SA, Santora L, Duncan L, Corbett-Detig R, Kapusinszky B, et al. Outbreak Associated with SARS-CoV-2 B.1.617.2 (Delta) Variant in an Elementary School — Marin County, California, May–June 2021. MMWR. Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. 2021;70(35):1214-1219. doi:10.15585/mmwr.mm7035e2

records.exposure_type: single index (teacher), repeated over <=5 school days (2 days while symptomatic)
records.exposure_duration_note: school days 17-21 May; hours in class not reported
records.geometry_note: five rows; 'all desks were separated by 6 ft' (1.83 m); seating chart in Fig. 1 of source
records.ventilation: portable HEPA filter in room; doors and windows left open
records.masks: students masked (high adherence); teacher unmasked when reading aloud
records.attack_rate_reported: 12/22 tested (55%); '50%' of 24 students; front two rows 8/10 (80%) vs back three rows 4/14 (28%), Fisher p = 0.036
records.spatial_pattern: monotone decrease with distance from the teacher's desk (two zones reported)
records.other_groups: second classroom (different grade) 6/14 tested; 4 siblings, 4 parents; 27 cases in total
records.quality_notes: 2 of 24 students untested (counted as non-cases in the row analysis). Row-level, not seat-level, numbers in text. Exposure hours not given. Children; Delta variant.

model_mapping.lattice: ~10 x 10 (5 rows of desks at 1.83 m spacing => ~9 m x 9 m; room size not reported)
model_mapping.T_days: 2-5 school days x ~6.5 h (17-21 May 2021); effectively first generation
model_mapping.mobility: students seated (D zone), teacher in podium zone (P)
model_mapping.role: calibration candidate for the classroom kernel OR held-out shape test
model_mapping.obstacles: hours not reported; masks on students; Delta variant; HEPA + open windows

records.setting: High school (grades 7-12), crowded classrooms 35-38 students in 39-49 m2

sources.citation: Stein-Zamir C, Abramson N, Shoob H, Libal E, Bitan M, Cardash T, et al. A large COVID-19 outbreak in a high school 10 days after schools' reopening, Israel, May 2020. Euro Surveill. 2020;25(29). doi:10.2807/1560-7917.ES.2020.25.29.2001352

records.exposure_type: two unlinked index students, ~8 school days, multi-class mixing
records.exposure_duration_note: ~8-9 school days at 6.3-6.7 h per day (38-40 h per 6-day week)
records.room_dimensions: class area 39-49 m2 (1.1-1.3 m2 per student)
records.geometry_note: floor_area_m2 is the midpoint of the reported range
records.ventilation: split air-conditioning per class running continuously (recirculating); windows not described
records.spatial_pattern: strong clustering by class: 20 cases in one 9th-grade class, 13 each in two others, 14 in one 7th-grade class
records.quality_notes: School-level denominators; per-class denominators only as class size range (35-38). Multi-generation over 10 days. No within-room positions.

model_mapping.lattice: 7 x 6 to 7 x 7 per classroom (39-49 m2); 30+ classrooms coupled through teachers/schoolyard
model_mapping.n_agents: 35-38 students + teacher per class; 1,164 students, 152 staff
model_mapping.mobility: seated; between-class coupling via teachers and breaks
model_mapping.role: held-out multi-generation test of the multi-room (scene-coupling) extension
model_mapping.obstacles: per-class denominators and positions not reported

records.setting: 20 elementary schools, classrooms with seats a median 3 ft (0.9 m) apart, masks worn

sources.citation: Hershow RB, Wu K, Lewis NM, Milne AT, Currie D, Smith AR, et al. Low SARS-CoV-2 Transmission in Elementary Schools — Salt Lake County, Utah, December 3, 2020–January 31, 2021. MMWR. Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. 2021;70(12):442-448. doi:10.15585/mmwr.mm7012e3

records.exposure_type: 51 index patients (40 students, 11 staff), school-day exposure of classroom contacts
records.exposure_duration_note: school days during infectious period; not quantified
records.ventilation: not quantified in text accessed
records.attack_rate_reported: 0.7% (5/728 tested susceptible school contacts); 1041 contacts, 735 tested, 12 cases of which 5 school-associated
records.spatial_pattern: 5 cases in 5 separate classrooms; no outbreaks (>=2 linked cases) detected
records.quality_notes: Pooled over 51 index cases: a per-index classroom secondary attack rate, the right quantity for a negative control. 70.6% of contacts tested.

model_mapping.lattice: scene default scaled to ~25 pupils (seat spacing 0.9 m)
model_mapping.T_days: 1-2 school days before isolation of the index
model_mapping.role: negative control (masked classrooms): model with mask factor must not exceed ~2%
model_mapping.obstacles: exposure hours and ventilation not quantified

records.setting: Suburban elementary school, 14 classrooms sharing a recirculating ventilation system

sources.citation: RILEY EC, MURPHY G, RILEY RL. AIRBORNE SPREAD OF MEASLES IN A SUBURBAN ELEMENTARY SCHOOL. American Journal of Epidemiology. 1978;107(5):421-432. doi:10.1093/oxfordjournals.aje.a112560

records.exposure_type: single index (2nd-grade girl), first generation
records.ventilation: high percentage of recirculated air (central system)
records.attack_rate_reported: 28 secondary cases in 14 different classrooms; 60 cases after two further generations; 97% of children vaccinated; index emitted ~93 quanta/min
records.spatial_pattern: secondary cases spread over 14 classrooms (not confined to the index's home room) -> building-scale airborne mixing
records.quality_notes: Abstract only: susceptible denominators not transcribed, so no attack rate. It is the origin of the quantum concept [riley1978airborne].

model_mapping.T_days: school days of one infectious period
model_mapping.role: qualitative only (shows need for a non-local/ventilation coupling term)

records.setting: Fitness dance classes, 5-22 students in a ~60 m2 room, 50 min intense exercise

sources.citation: Jang S, Han SH, Rhee JY. Cluster of Coronavirus Disease Associated with Fitness Dance Classes, South Korea. Emerging Infectious Diseases. 2020;26(8):1917-1920. doi:10.3201/eid2608.200633

records.exposure_type: 8 infected instructors teaching classes twice weekly for ~1 week
records.exposure_duration_note: 50 min per class, 2 classes per week
records.ventilation: not reported
records.index_case: 8 instructors infected at a 4-h workshop on 15 Feb
records.attack_rate_reported: 26.3% (95% CI 20.9-32.5%) among 217 students exposed in 12 facilities
records.spatial_pattern: none within rooms; no cases in classes with <5 participants or in low-intensity (Pilates/yoga) classes of 7-8 in the same room
records.other_groups: secondary attack rate among 830 close contacts 4.10%
records.quality_notes: n_infected = 57 is DERIVED from 26.3% x 217 (count not printed in main text). High-exertion breathing: an upper-range analogue for classrooms.

model_mapping.T_days: 50 min per class (0.035 d), 2 classes per week
observables: no cases in classes with < 5 participants or low-intensity classes
model_mapping.role: held-out level test (density and activity dependence)

records.setting: Coach bus, 15 rows (3+2 seats), air conditioning in recirculation/heating mode

sources.access: publisher's full-text page (JAMA Netw) as an automated text extraction; abstract via Europe PMC
sources.citation: Shen Y, Li C, Dong H, Wang Z, Martinez L, Sun Z, et al. Community Outbreak Investigation of SARS-CoV-2 Transmission Among Bus Riders in Eastern China. JAMA Internal Medicine. 2020;180(12):1665. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2020.5225

records.exposure_type: single index, single day, two 50-min rides
records.geometry_note: index in middle seat of the 3-seat side, row 8; seat map in source figure (not digitized)
records.ventilation: air conditioning on indoor recirculation; 4 openable windows (2 per side)
records.attack_rate_reported: 24/68 = 35.3% incl. index; 23/67 = 34.3% excl. index
records.spatial_pattern: No significant distance gradient: rows 5-11 (within ~2 m) 14/33 vs other rows 9/34, RR 1.6 (0.8-3.2); rows 6-10 11/23 vs others 12/44, RR 1.8 (0.9-3.3). Window-side passengers (3-seat side) and those near the door largely spared.
records.other_groups: unexposed bus 1: 0/60; other attendees of the same 150-min outdoor event: 7/172 (4.1%)
records.quality_notes: Natural control group (bus 1). Exposure also includes the shared worship event (controlled for by 7/172). Bus dimensions not printed.

model_mapping.lattice: 23 x 5 (15 rows x 0.75 m = 11.25 m; width ~2.5 m assumed, not reported)
model_mapping.index_position: known: row 8, middle seat of 3-seat side
model_mapping.role: held-out shape + level test
model_mapping.obstacles: bus width/height not printed; seat-level map not digitized

records.setting: Long-distance coach, 11.3 m x 2.5 m, 49 seats, windows closed

sources.citation: Luo K, Lei Z, Hai Z, Xiao S, Rui J, Yang H, et al. Transmission of SARS-CoV-2 in Public Transportation Vehicles: A Case Study in Hunan Province, China. Open Forum Infectious Diseases. 2020;7(10):ofaa430. doi:10.1093/ofid/ofaa430

Ou C, Hu S, Luo K, Yang H, Hang J, Cheng P, et al. Insufficient ventilation led to a probable long-range airborne transmission of SARS-CoV-2 on two buses. Building and Environment. 2022;207:108414. doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2021.108414

records.exposure_type: single index (pre-symptomatic), single ride
records.room_dimensions: 11.3 m x 2.5 m (Luo 2020); air volume 60.42 m3 (Ou 2022)
records.geometry_note: index in second rear row (Luo) ; seat-numbered plan in Ou 2022 Fig. 2 (not digitized)
records.ventilation: measured time-averaged 1.72 L/s per person (Ou 2022); 0.62 ACH when idling
records.attack_rate_reported: Luo 2020: pooled 9/(48+12) = 15.0% (95% CI 6-24%) over both vehicles; Ou 2022: 7/46 = 15.2% on this coach
records.spatial_pattern: No distance gradient: rear rows 8-13 3/19 (15.8%) vs front rows 1-7 4/26 (15.4%); driver side 6/24 vs opposite side 1/20 (Ou 2022). Farthest infectees ~4.5 m (7 rows) from index (Luo 2020).
records.other_groups: 1 further case on the return trip of the same coach 30 min later (seat near the index's former seat)
records.quality_notes: Two investigations of the same event give different denominators (48 vs 46) and durations (150 vs 200 min). Ventilation measured post hoc with tracer gas.

observables: driver side vs opposite side 6/24 vs 1/20
model_mapping.role: held-out shape + level test (measured ventilation 1.72 L/s per person)
model_mapping.obstacles: two reports disagree on denominator and duration

records.setting: Minibus, 5.5 m x 2.5 m, 18 seats, windows mostly closed

sources.citation: Luo K, Lei Z, Hai Z, Xiao S, Rui J, Yang H, et al. Transmission of SARS-CoV-2 in Public Transportation Vehicles: A Case Study in Hunan Province, China. Open Forum Infectious Diseases. 2020;7(10):ofaa430. doi:10.1093/ofid/ofaa430

Ou C, Hu S, Luo K, Yang H, Hang J, Cheng P, et al. Insufficient ventilation led to a probable long-range airborne transmission of SARS-CoV-2 on two buses. Building and Environment. 2022;207:108414. doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2021.108414

records.exposure_type: single index (same person as T2), single ride
records.room_dimensions: 5.5 m x 2.5 m; air volume 21.69 m3 (Ou 2022)
records.ventilation: measured time-averaged 3.22 L/s per person (Ou 2022)
records.attack_rate_reported: 2/12 (Luo 2020: '2 out of 12 passengers (including the driver)'); Ou 2022: 2/17 = 11.8%
records.spatial_pattern: infectees 1 row (~1.5 m) and 3 rows (~4.5 m) from the index
records.quality_notes: Denominator differs between the two reports (12 vs 17). Very small n.

model_mapping.role: held-out level test (same index as T2: tests duration + ventilation scaling with infectiousness fixed)

records.setting: High-speed train second-class coaches (3+2 seats per row); pooled contact-tracing cohort

sources.access: publisher's full-text page (OUP) as an automated text extraction; abstract via Europe PMC
sources.citation: Hu M, Lin H, Wang J, Xu C, Tatem AJ, Meng B, et al. Risk of Coronavirus Disease 2019 Transmission in Train Passengers: an Epidemiological and Modeling Study. Clinical Infectious Diseases. 2021;72(4):604-610. doi:10.1093/cid/ciaa1057

records.exposure_type: 2,334 index patients; co-travel 0.13-13.8 h (mean 2.1 h, SD 1.8)
records.room_dimensions: seat width ~0.5 m; row spacing reported as ~0.4 m
records.geometry_note: contacts defined as within 3 rows of the index; 5 column offsets (incl. aisle)
records.ventilation: not reported
records.attack_rate_reported: 0.32% (95% CI 0.29-0.37%); adjacent seat 3.5% (2.9-4.3%); same row 1.5% (1.3-1.8%); 1/2/3 rows away 0.14/0.18/0.08%; +0.15 %-points per hour overall, +1.3 per hour adjacent
records.spatial_pattern: steep decay within the row (3.53 -> 1.65 -> 0.38% over 1-3 seats) and an order-of-magnitude drop between rows; non-zero plateau ~0.1% at 2-3 rows
records.other_groups: later occupant of the index's seat: 1/1342 (0.075%)
records.quality_notes: Largest distance-resolved dataset, but cell denominators were not transcribed (percentages + CIs only). Row-0 cell alignment of Table 1 was reconstructed. Early-pandemic ascertainment (symptomatic testing) biases attack rates downward.
derived: alignment of the row-0 cells of Table 1

model_mapping.lattice: 6 columns (A B C aisle D F) x rows of one coach (rows per coach not reported); 1 site per seat (0.5 m wide); row spacing per source 0.4 m
model_mapping.n_agents: full coach (seat count not reported in source)
model_mapping.index_position: origin of the (d_row, d_col) offset matrix
observables: 23-cell attack-rate matrix by (rows apart, columns apart)
model_mapping.role: CALIBRATION of the distance kernel and of the duration dependence
model_mapping.obstacles: cell denominators not transcribed; 0.4 m row spacing implausible as seat pitch

records.setting: Long-haul flight, business-class cabin (28 seats, 21 occupied)

sources.citation: Khanh NC, Thai PQ, Quach HL, Thi NAH, Dinh PC, Duong TN, et al. Transmission of SARS-CoV 2 During Long-Haul Flight. Emerging Infectious Diseases. 2020;26(11):2617-2624. doi:10.3201/eid2611.203299

records.exposure_type: single symptomatic index, single flight
records.ventilation: aircraft cabin (HEPA recirculation; not quantified)
records.attack_rate_reported: business class 13/21 = 62% incl. index; '≤2 seats away' 11/12 (92%) vs '>2 seats away' 1/8 (13%), RR 7.3 (1.2-46.2)
records.spatial_pattern: sharp proximity effect within the cabin; no spread to premium economy 0/35; economy 2/145; crew 1/16
records.quality_notes: 84% of passengers traced. Economy cases may be unrelated. High air-change cabin: not a carriage, but the only 10-h seat-resolved record.

model_mapping.lattice: business cabin 28 seats (layout in source Fig. 1, not digitized)
model_mapping.role: held-out shape test (long duration)
model_mapping.obstacles: cabin geometry not transcribed; cabin air exchange far higher than metro

records.exposure_type: single index, single event

records.spatial_pattern: not in abstract

records.setting: National cluster surveillance; commuter rail as a venue category

sources.citation: Furuse Y, Sando E, Tsuchiya N, Miyahara R, Yasuda I, Ko YK, et al. Clusters of Coronavirus Disease in Communities, Japan, January–April 2020. Emerging Infectious Diseases. 2020;26(9):2176-2179. doi:10.3201/eid2609.202272

records.exposure_type: surveillance (clusters of >=5 cases with a common venue)
records.attack_rate_reported: 61 clusters among 3,184 cases: 18 healthcare, 10 other care, 10 restaurants/bars, 8 workplaces, 7 music events, 5 gyms, 2 ceremonies, 1 transport-related (an airplane); no cluster is attributed to trains or stations
records.spatial_pattern: n/a
records.quality_notes: Absence of detected clusters is weak evidence: exposure on anonymous mass transit is almost never traceable. No documented metro-carriage outbreak with denominators was found in this search.

records.setting: Restaurant dining floor, 18 tables, 89 patrons, fan-coil air conditioning without outdoor air

sources.citation: Li Y, Qian H, Hang J, Chen X, Cheng P, Ling H, et al. Probable airborne transmission of SARS-CoV-2 in a poorly ventilated restaurant. Building and Environment. 2021;196:107788. doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2021.107788

Lu J, Gu J, Li K, Xu C, Su W, Lai Z, et al. COVID-19 Outbreak Associated with Air Conditioning in Restaurant, Guangzhou, China, 2020. Emerging Infectious Diseases. 2020;26(7):1628-1631. doi:10.3201/eid2607.200764

records.exposure_type: single index, single lunch
records.exposure_duration_note: index table present 82 min (12:01-13:23); overlap 53 min (table B), 75 min (table C; Lu 2020 gives 73 min), 23-82 min for others
records.geometry_note: table plan with seat positions in Li 2021 Fig. 1; distances index-to-infected up to 4.6 m; 1.55 m2 per patron
records.ventilation: measured 0.56-0.77 ACH = 0.75-1.04 L/s per patron (tracer decay); 5 fan-coil units, no outdoor air supply
records.attack_rate_reported: 10/89 = 11.24% incl. table A; non-A tables 5/79; immediate neighbouring tables 5/16 (31.25%) vs remote tables 0/63; air-conditioning zone ABC 5/11 (45.45%) vs other zone 0/68
records.spatial_pattern: all infections inside one air-conditioning recirculation zone; none among 68 patrons elsewhere or 8 staff; not ordered by distance within the zone (the 2 patrons of table C closest to A were not infected)
records.other_groups: index's own table (family, travelled together): 4 of 9 others infected - excluded from the secondary attack rate
records.quality_notes: Best-documented single event (video-verified seating, measured ventilation, per-table exposure times). Lu 2020 counts 83 customers + 8 staff = 91 persons; Li 2021 counts 89 patrons. Table-A infections cannot be separated from household/travel exposure.

model_mapping.T_days: per-table exposure 48-89 min (index table 82 min = 0.057 d)
model_mapping.index_position: known: seat A1 at table A (window side)
observables: per-table attack rates (18 tables) vs per-table exposure time
CFD/tracer-normalised exposure per table as an independent covariate
model_mapping.role: CALIBRATION candidate (best single event) or primary held-out test
model_mapping.obstacles: airflow zoning (not distance) organises the risk; table A confounded by household exposure

records.setting: Restaurant, 9.2 m x 10.5 m, no windows or ventilation system, two ceiling air conditioners

sources.citation: Kwon KS, Park JI, Park YJ, Jung DM, Ryu KW, Lee JH. Evidence of Long-Distance Droplet Transmission of SARS-CoV-2 by Direct Air Flow in a Restaurant in Korea. Journal of Korean Medical Science. 2020;35(46):e415. doi:10.3346/jkms.2020.35.e415

records.exposure_type: single index (visitor), single visit
records.exposure_duration_note: overlaps of 5 min (case A) and 21 min (case C) with the infector
records.geometry_note: air conditioners 3.2 m above floor; measured air speed 1.0-1.2 m/s along the infector-infectee path
records.ventilation: no windows, no ventilation system; directed air-conditioner jet
records.spatial_pattern: both infectees downstream in the air-conditioner jet at 6.5 m (5 min) and 4.8 m (21 min); nobody outside the airflow path infected
records.quality_notes: CCTV-verified positions and timings. n = 13. Demonstrates directed (advective) long-range transmission in minutes.

model_mapping.T_days: 5 min and 21 min overlaps (0.0035 d, 0.015 d)
observables: 2/13 infected at 4.8 m and 6.5 m within 5-21 min
model_mapping.role: stress test: advective transport (not representable by isotropic diffusion)

records.exposure_type: single index, single 2.5-h rehearsal
records.exposure_duration_note: 40 min together, 50 min sectionals, 15 min break, 45 min together

records.geometry_note: chairs 6-10 in (15-25 cm) apart; nobody within 3 m in front of the index
records.ventilation: estimated 0.3-1.0 h-1 (central estimate 0.7 h-1) from furnace heat balance; not measured
records.attack_rate_reported: 86.7% (52/60; 32 confirmed + 20 probable); 53.3% confirmed only (32/60)
records.spatial_pattern: 'absence of any strong pattern in the spatial distribution of secondary cases' (Miller 2021); seat map withheld for privacy

records.exposure_type: single index, four ~1-h services on 3 days

records.geometry_note: circular church with high conical roof; seat positions from video
records.ventilation: apex ventilation off, doors/windows largely closed, wall fans off ('minimal ventilation')
records.spatial_pattern: all 12 secondary cases sat within one 70-degree sector, 1-15 m from (and below) the index; none in other sectors
